## Subjective

55yo F, established patient with longstanding HTN, hyperlipidemia, and now presenting with multi-faceted concerns (location: chest discomfort + right shoulder pain; quality: chest pressure-like, shoulder dull aching; severity: chest 4/10, shoulder 5/10; duration: chest 1 week intermittent, shoulder 3 weeks progressive; timing: chest with exertion, shoulder constant; context: shoulder triggered after gardening; modifying factors: chest improves with rest, shoulder worse with overhead movement; associated symptoms: occasional fatigue, no SOB, no palpitations, no syncope).

Patient reports compliance with home BP monitoring, BPs at home running 142-156/86-94 over the past 3 weeks (up from 128-138/76-82 over preceding months). Reports adherence to lisinopril 10mg daily and atorvastatin 20mg daily, both consistently for 4+ years. No reports of dietary changes that could explain BP rise; recently started new exercise routine but BP rise preceded that.

Cardiac sx: occasional retrosternal pressure-like sensation with stair-climbing, lasts 5-10 min, relieved with rest. Has not awakened her at night. Denies syncope, presyncope, palpitations, diaphoresis.

Right shoulder: gradual onset 3 weeks ago following several days of yard work. Localized to right shoulder, no neck radiation, no numbness/tingling distally. Worse with reaching overhead. Some night pain when sleeping on right side.

PMH: Essential hypertension since age 45, hyperlipidemia since age 52, h/o iron deficiency anemia (resolved 2020). Tobacco never. EtOH occasional (1-2 drinks/wk). Surgical history: appendectomy 1985, cholecystectomy 2010.

FHx: Father - HTN, MI age 71 (deceased CHF age 78). Mother - HTN, alive age 82. Sibling - hyperlipidemia.

SHx: Married, lives with spouse. Retired teacher. Walks 30 min daily. Diet: balanced, low salt per discussion. Occupational stress low currently. Sleep: 7-8 hr nightly, no apnea sx.

Constitutional: denies fever, weight change, fatigue. CV: chest pressure as above, denies palpitations, syncope. Resp: denies cough, SOB, hemoptysis. GI: denies nausea, abdominal pain. MSK: shoulder pain as above. Neuro: denies headache, dizziness, weakness.

## Objective

VS: BP 158/92 (rechecked 152/88), HR 78 (regular), RR 16, T 98.4°F, SpO2 98% on RA, BMI 26.4. Gen: anxious-appearing but in no acute distress. HEENT: anicteric, oropharynx unremarkable, no carotid bruit. Cardiac: RRR no m/r/g, no S3 or S4, no JVD. Lungs: CTAB throughout, no wheezing or crackles. Abdomen: soft, non-tender, no HSM, bowel sounds normal. Extremities: no edema, distal pulses 2+ bilaterally, capillary refill <2s. MSK right shoulder: mild tenderness over supraspinatus tendon insertion, no swelling, no warmth, ROM full but limited at end-range abduction by pain, Hawkins test mildly positive, Empty Can test mildly positive, no atrophy. Skin: no rash. Neuro: A&O×3, CN II-XII intact, motor strength 5/5 bilateral upper and lower extremities, sensation intact throughout, gait normal.

## Assessment

1. Hypertension, suboptimally controlled (I10) — recent home BP rise to 142-156/86-94, repeatable in office
2. Atypical chest discomfort with exertion (R07.9) — concern for possible angina vs musculoskeletal contribution
3. Right shoulder pain, likely rotator cuff tendinopathy (M75.101)
4. Hyperlipidemia (E78.5) — currently on therapy

## Plan

Hypertension intensification: increased lisinopril from 10mg to 20mg daily. Continue home BP log, ideally 2x daily for 2 weeks. Counseled on dietary salt awareness, hydration. F/u 2 weeks.

Chest discomfort workup: EKG performed in office today — normal sinus rhythm without ST changes or abnormalities. Discussed risk stratification given new HTN + family history. Stress test ordered — patient will schedule. Counseled patient to call/return immediately for: chest pain at rest, pain lasting >10 min, radiation to jaw or arm, associated SOB, syncope, or diaphoresis. Started ASA 81mg daily empirically pending workup. Lipid panel ordered today.

Right shoulder: Likely rotator cuff tendinopathy. Discussed conservative management: relative rest from overhead activities, OTC ibuprofen 600mg q8h with food x 7-10 days, gentle scapular stabilization exercises, ice 15 min q4h PRN. Avoid sleeping on right side. F/u 3 weeks if not improving — would consider PT referral or cortisone injection. Return precautions: significant weakness, persistent night pain, deformity.

Patient education: comprehensive review of warning signs. F/u 2 weeks for BP recheck and stress test results. F/u 3 weeks for shoulder reassessment.
